connector: The Dwarf has started his story, and it’s a story inside a story: the four children are sitting by the fire, listening, while we go back to a castle and a boy named Caspian. Keep two lists as you read today: who is with Caspian, and who is against him.

a.raw: the nurse told him about old narnia but miraz sent her away
a.fixed: The nurse told him about Old Narnia, but Miraz sent her away.
a.why: Capitals start the sentence and name Old Narnia and Miraz; a comma comes before but because it joins two complete sentences; a period ends it.

b.raw: caspian loved history so doctor cornelius taught him in secret
b.fixed: Caspian loved history, so Doctor Cornelius taught him in secret.
b.why: Capitals on Caspian and Doctor Cornelius; a comma before so, which joins a cause to what it led to; a period ends it.

notes.wordParts: Latin bases: port = carry, tract = pull or draw, struct = build: transport, attract, construct, instructed.
notes.grammar: But and so join two complete sentences. But says the second part goes against what you expected; so says the second part happens because of the first. Put a comma before each.
notes.spelling: Suffix rules: drop the silent e (hope + ing = hoping); change y to i (empty + er = emptier); double the last consonant when the last syllable is stressed (begin + ing = beginning, but visit + ing = visiting).

wordgame.h: Bases that carry, pull and build
wordgame.voice: Tap a word base, then the word it belongs in. Or drag the base onto the word.

why.t: The treasure chamber at Cair Paravel is still waiting for its treasures. This week Caspian learns that the old stories are true, and the Old Narnians come out of hiding one by one. Each word you build sets one more treasure in its place. This week’s Latin bases: port (carry), tract (pull) and struct (build).

wordgame.winDay: More treasures are back in their niches.
wordgame.win: Four treasures are back in their niches. port = carry, tract = pull, struct = build.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. Chapter 4 happens in Miraz’s castle, where the old stories are a secret. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Miraz asks what more anyone could wish for than to be King. Caspian answers, “All the same, I do wish,” and tells his uncle the truth: he wishes he could have lived in the Old Days.
items.why: Caspian says what he really thinks, even to the King.
items.hint: Does Caspian hide what he wishes?

items.t: Doctor Cornelius whispers that if the King found him telling Caspian secrets, he would lose his head. He goes on teaching Caspian the truth anyway.
items.why: He takes a terrible risk so Caspian can know the truth.
items.hint: What could happen to the Doctor?

items.t: On the tower, the Doctor says Caspian can help the hidden Old Narnians when he is King. Caspian says, “I do, I do. But how can I help?”
items.why: Caspian wants to help people who need it.

morphology.label: Nell · bases that carry, pull and build

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. The Dwarf is telling the children a story, and now we hear it too. It’s about a boy who grew up in a castle where the old stories were forbidden. Today’s question: why would the truth ever need to be hidden?
transcripts.read: Keep two lists as you read. Everyone who helps Caspian goes on one. Everyone who controls him goes on the other. If you can’t tell yet, write the name with a question mark. Watch the nurse, the King, and the Doctor with the great spectacles.
transcripts.morphology: Some words are built on old Latin bases. Port means carry, so transport carries something across. Tract means pull, so extract pulls something out. Struct means build, so construct builds something together. Find the base, ask what it does, and set a treasure back in its place.
